recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-10236; future geolocation definition changes should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack.
issue_request: FHIR-10236 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked for geocode information to be usable wherever Address is used, and the accepted resolution was to define a geolocation extension on Address with latitude and longitude components plus a comment that it can be further extended for identifiers, confidence, altitude, and related metadata.
initial_application: Jira records the original application as svn revision 8941. Imported git history shows the requested geolocation extension rows in the former core general-extensions spreadsheet before the later R5 standard-extension extraction removed those definitions from core source.
additional_context: The authoritative current definition is in the FHIR Extension Pack. It has context Address, defines latitude and longitude slices, and retains the requested extensibility comment. Later FHIR-43290 confirmed the extension is intended for Address generally rather than only Location; FHIR-42974 only removed dangling note references from latitude and longitude definitions.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current core source links defined-extension examples through the extension-pack location and uses the canonical geolocation extension in bundle examples, while the extension definition itself correctly lives outside core.

related_jiras.note: Published FHIR-extensions clarification changed Location-specific wording to address-focused wording, confirming the Address-wide interpretation.
Published FHIR-extensions correction removed dangling note references from latitude and longitude definitions without changing the FHIR-10236 semantics.
